rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly on this small (10.5 KB text, 46-function) pointer- and float-heavy Olden benchmark, so the table now leans into obfuscation while budgeting costs: SUB gets the strongest security/diversity weights since voronoi is dominated by geometric arithmetic (vector.c, circle_center, triangulation math) where instruction substitution is cheap, safe, and highly resistant-raising; FLA stays high because the large control-flow-dense functions (do_merge ~2 KB, output_voronoi_diagram ~1.9 KB, build_delaunay) are ideal flattening targets, with moderate cost weights reflecting their hot loops; BCF is raised moderately for bogus-path depth on those same functions but its runtime weight is kept lower since voronoi's Delaunay/merge loops are runtime-sensitive; SPLIT is weighted toward diversity at minimal cost and acts as a force multiplier for FLA by creating more basic blocks to flatten; IBR gets elevated diversity weight to convert the branch-heavy merge/sweep logic into indirect control flow, complicating static CFG recovery; IGV is kept mid-range since voronoi has few global constants to hide but parameterized bounds/tables still benefit; ICALL stays lowest of the set because indirect-call transformation on a small program adds call-overhead and correctness risk (function-pointer-heavy Olden code) with limited payoff. Overall the cost weights are held just below the security weights so feature-matched functions are aggressively transformed, while the still-substantial CorrectnessRisk weights preserve the pass gate that kept round 1 correct.
